newsitem.title: USA: Atmos sees United Cities deal dilutive in 1st year.
newsitem.headline: Atmos sees United Cities deal dilutive in 1st year.

text.p: Atmos Energy Corp expects its acquisition of United Cities Gas Co to bring costs of $10-15 million and have a dilutive effect on earnings in the first year, company executives said.

"It will be dilutive because it is a pooling, and we'll be expensing all of the merger costs," Vice President and Chief Financial Officer James Purser told Reuters. "It will be an expensive transaction to complete."
Purser said the merger between the two natural gas companies will be completed in March 1997, and its benefits should kick in from early 1998.
"It will take about a year to get all the plans worked out ... and it will be positive from there on in," Purser said.
Shareholders of Dallas-based Atmos and Brentwood, Minn.-based United Cities earlier on Tuesday approved the merger in separate meetings.
Under the deal, United Cities will be merged into Atmos with one share of Atmos being exchanged for each share of United Cities.
Atmos is to issue about 13.35 million new shares of common stock in order to carry out the deal, bringing its total number of outstanding shares to about 29.4 million.

Atmos President and Chief Operating Officer Robert Stephens said the merger will boost its customer base from 674,000 currently to over 1 million with the combined company operating in 13 states from Georgia and North and South Carolina in the Southeast, across the Midwest and to the western slopes of the Rocky Mountains.
He said the merger reflects the process of consolidation in the energy industry and that Atmos will likely be making further acquisitions in the future.
"We don't think this is our last deal by any stretch," Stephens said. "We don't have any specific plans but we believe it is a good strategy to have acquisition growth as well as internal growth."
Regulatory approvals for the Atmos-United Cities merger are pending in eight states.
Atmos shares were down 1/8 at 22-7/8 in afternoon trade on the New York Stock Exchange while United Cities shares were down 1/4 to 21-1/4 on the Nasdaq National Market.
